exact_claim: For any reviewed fixed-reference Q static crossing, choose an interior regular-side time tube, one nonzero smooth compact profile f, positive physical units Psi,L, and c_tau=1/sqrt(tau). The states phi=phi0+Psi sqrt(epsilon) f((x-x0-c_tau t)/(L epsilon)), n=rho, j=0, chi=chi0 have uniformly bounded finite full energy and weakly convergent derivatives. Every actual mass/source/scale/matter and combined momentum residual vanishes in its explicitly declared weak space, yet their full nonlinear energy and momentum/stress fluxes acquire nonzero moving concentration measures. The initial energy defect is E_*=Psi² integral f′²/(C L)>0. This refutes only the stated weak-residual/bounded-energy compactness implication, not exact solutions or strongly energy-prepared approximations. A Psi epsilon amplitude control has vanishing relative energy and no defect; strong L2 field derivatives suffice to identify fluxes in the fixed-density/scale class.
new_assumptions: Select a compact interior interval on one regular side of the reviewed crossing and a finite time slab for which the traveling support remains there.
Fix one smooth nonzero compact profile, positive potential/length units and the inherited positive tau; no couplings are changed.
Approximate states are measured only in the explicit uniform-time H^-1, L1, Lip* or spacetime distributional residual spaces stated in DERIVATION.
The main sequence is weakly prepared in field derivatives but has a nonzero initial energy and momentum concentration.
The sufficient strong compactness criterion is confined to the fixed-density/scale class; general fluid/scale fluxes require further integrability.
